chapter: Learning the trombone and jam sessions
title: Minton's, Monroe's and carrying your own rhythm section
summary: Minton's and Monroe's held sessions, and horn players brought their own rhythm sections, but real jams meant playing with strangers.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Up at Minton's -- used to go at Minton's. Same thing. But even before modern jazz got up at Minton's, they used to run the sessions up there. A lot of guys used to go. I used to go up there and play a lot. But all over. They had these things on 52nd Street, all around. But way before 52nd Street these things because -- and Monroe's Uptown House -- they used to -- that was all they did up there was jam all the time.

I've heard that some of the major horn players used to carry their own rhythm sections with them for sessions. They'd go out after work and challenge somebody, but they'd bring along their own rhythm.
Yeah, they used to do that. A lot of them used to do that.
Do you remember who? I understand
Ben Webster had his own, and who else?
Coleman Hawkins -- (Unintelligible). Hawk used this (unintelligible) is before Ben, and Blanche Calloway. Guys were doing that around New York.
Do you remember who and who they had with them?

Well, I don't remember exactly who was with him but they would -- especially they would have their own bass and piano player with them. It probably would be whoever they were working with at that particular time because the guys knew what they were playing, you know. For instance, if I'm working in say a little band on 52nd Street every night, well, they'd get into what I was playing. If I went out to jam, I could take them out with me. I'd say come on, let's go over to so and so place and play. This was just like taking your own group with you almost.

Because what you were playing -- they knew exactly what you were doing. So, you didn't have no problem. But when they really were jamming good though, guys wouldn't do that. They'd just take anybody, you know, that could play. I thought those were the most challenging times when I guy would just play with somebody that he didn't play

with all the time. That was the real challenge. It was easy to play with somebody you play with every night, but the real sessions, they wouldn't let nobody do that in most of the real sessions. You had to play with what was there and do your best with it.
